**Question:** What is the expected output for `user@1.2.3.4`, where the text looks like an email address but its domain is a dotted number? (FR-007, FR-019)

**Why it matters:** The Edge Cases section says this is "redacted" but not *as what*, and the two plausible answers produce different output — so an acceptance test can't be written yet. Under the current rules as literally stated, the email pattern can't match (FR-007 requires the domain to end in at least two letters), so the address part alone would be caught, giving `user@[IP]`.

**Recommended:** Option A — it is what the requirements as written already produce, needs no rule changes, and still removes the sensitive network address; the leftover `user@` is a username fragment, which is not one of the three identifier types this feature covers.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | `user@[IP]` — the email rule does not match a numeric domain, so the IPv4 rule redacts the address and the `user@` prefix stays |
| B | `[EMAIL]` — widen the email rule to also accept a dotted-quad domain, so the whole thing is one email match |
| C | `user@[IP]` today, but add a note that swallowing the local part is a known limitation to revisit |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
